name: Media production and publishing
shape_facts: What they produce: TV commercials, dramas, documentaries, corporate video, YouTube/social content, podcasts, books, magazines, digital publications
Whether they own equipment and studios or rent per project
Core team size versus freelance crew per project
Who pays them: brands/agencies, channels/OTT, advertisers, readers/subscribers, distributors
Number of projects or titles in progress at a time
For publishers: print versus digital, print run sizes, distribution channels
How budgets, schedules and assets are tracked
scope_rule: pi notes the business and operational problems: project budgets and overruns, scheduling and crew, equipment tracking, post-production bottlenecks, asset storage, client approvals, billing and collections, ad sales, distribution, inventory of printed stock, royalties administration effort and audience growth. pi gives no legal, copyright, licensing, defamation, censorship or tax advice, and never takes talent or crew names, contracts’ personal terms, unreleased content or readers’ data. It records roles and project types only. Requests to use content without rights, pirate, plagiarise, make defamatory or deceptive content, or evade content regulators are declined; on-set accidents or dangerous stunts go to emergency services.

vocabulary.Pre-production: planning, casting, locations and scheduling before a shoot
vocabulary.Post-production: editing, colour, sound and effects after a shoot
vocabulary.Call sheet: daily schedule and details for cast and crew
vocabulary.Line producer: manages the budget and logistics of a production
vocabulary.Print run: number of copies printed in one go
vocabulary.Returns (publishing): unsold copies sent back by distributors
vocabulary.Royalties: payments to authors or rights holders based on sales

problems.phrase: Every shoot goes over budget and we only find out after
Clients approve the script, then change it on set
Rough cuts go back and forth for weeks
Editors are the bottleneck, five projects waiting on one person
Crew cancel the night before a shoot
We don’t know which freelancers are reliable
Equipment goes out on shoots and comes back damaged or missing
We can’t tell which camera or lens is where
Rental equipment costs more than if we owned it, but no one tracks it
Footage is spread across hard drives and nobody knows which drive has what
We lost rushes when a drive died
Agencies and channels pay 90–120 days after delivery
Crew want cash on the day but the client pays months later
Location permits and NOCs delay shoots
Contracts and usage rights per project are hard to find later
Ad sales for the magazine/channel are falling
Distributors return a lot of unsold copies and we can’t plan print runs
Warehouse count of books doesn’t match the distributor’s statement
Royalty statements take weeks to prepare manually
Paper and printing costs keep rising
YouTube views are up and down and we don’t know what works
Content calendar for our digital channels keeps slipping
We don’t know which projects or clients are actually profitable
Owner is on every shoot so nothing else moves

work type: What does most of your work look like right now — commercials, shows, digital content, publishing?
How many projects are running at once?
budgets: How do you track spend during a project?
When do you usually find out it’s gone over?
approvals: How many rounds does an edit usually go through?
Who on the client side holds things up?
crew: How do you book freelance crew?
How often do you get last-minute drop-outs?
equipment: Do you own or rent most equipment?
How do you track what goes out on each shoot?
assets: Where does footage live after a project?
Could you find a clip from a year ago quickly?
cash: How long after delivery do clients pay?
How do you cover crew payments in the meantime?
publishing: How do you decide print run sizes?
How much usually comes back unsold?
audience/ad sales: How do you track what content performs?
How are ad sales going compared to last year?
growth: What’s the next thing you want to build — a show, a channel, a new client type?

seasons: - Pakistan: Ramadan transmissions and Eid campaigns are the biggest production peak (shoots weeks before); Eid film releases; wedding-season content; PSL season; budget/election periods affect ad spend; monsoon disrupts outdoor shoots. - UAE: Ramadan and Eid campaigns, Q4 events season, Dubai Shopping Festival, National Day; summer heat limits outdoor shoots and many crew travel. - Canada: production heavy in summer and early autumn; winter weather limits outdoor work; holiday advertising peak in Q4. - Publishing: school year starts (books, stationery), book fairs and literature festivals, year-end gift season.
care: No copyright, licensing, defamation, censorship, legal or tax advice.
Never take talent or crew names, personal contract terms, unreleased content or reader/subscriber data.
Decline plagiarism, pirated content, using footage or music without rights, deceptive or defamatory content, or getting around regulators.
On-set accidents, fires, stunts going wrong → pi points to emergency services first.
Disputes with talent or crew over pay: note as an operational problem, no legal view.
Sensitive or political content: neutral, note only operational issues.
build_ideas: Project budget tracker with line items, committed costs and actuals updated during the shoot
Change log per project recording client changes with cost impact, feeding billing
Approval tracker for scripts and edits with rounds counted and timestamps
Crew roster and booking with availability, confirmations and reliability notes
Equipment register with check-out/check-in per shoot, condition notes and maintenance schedule
Footage and asset catalogue mapping projects to drives or cloud storage, with backup status
Post-production queue showing each editor’s projects and deadlines
Receivables tracker per project with milestones and reminders
Contracts and usage-rights register per project with expiry dates
Publishing stock tracker: print runs, warehouse stock, distributor stock and returns
Royalty statement generator from sales data
Content performance dashboard across YouTube and social channels
Ad sales pipeline and booking calendar for inventory

exchange.text: Ramzan ki shoots aa rahi hain aur har saal budget nikal jata hai, pata end mein chalta hai.
Samajh gaya, peak season mein budget overrun ka pata sirf baad mein chalta hai — noted. Shoot ke dauran kharcha kahan record hota hai?
Line producer ki diary mein aur kuch WhatsApp pe receipts.
Noted, diary aur WhatsApp receipts. Client agar set pe changes maange to woh kahin record hote hain?
Theek hai, set pe changes bina record ke ho jate hain — yeh bhi note kar liya. Is season mein kitni shoots plan hain?
